sections.content: How many people stayed in Hazel Grove after gaining qualifications?

Hazel Grove is a small town in the North West. Hazel Grove does not have its own university.

Hazel Grove has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Hazel Grove ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 880 state-school pupils from Hazel Grove who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 340 (39%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 310 (35%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Hazel Grove to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Hazel Grove's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Hazel Grove in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Hazel Grove move to?

Of Hazel Grove's graduates, 140 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 85 of those graduates (61%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Hazel Grove's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 120 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 90 of those qualified non-graduates (75%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Hazel Grove's GCSE cohort:

  • 50 graduates left the North West
  • 25 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of graduates and 27% of qualified non-graduates living in Hazel Grove had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 280 graduates and 260 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Hazel Grove. This is compared with the 340 graduates and 310 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 71% of the graduates had also lived in Hazel Grove as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Hazel Grove in 2018 to 2019, 73% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 27% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
